cells.tense: The water in you is still, and the accounting underneath it is honest now.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Take the thing you already understand and read the hardest part of it again, slow, no deciding. Once is enough, then stop. If it stays flat, that is what it is; if it opens, you will see which way.
cells.core:
There is a steadiness in you that people can stand near without having to brace, and right now it is fair — the feeling is deep enough to think from and the reckoning underneath it is honest. You are not choosing between possibilities yet. You are letting the calm be full, and that is the work at this stage, not a pause before it.

Take the thing you already understand and read the hardest part of it again. Once, slow, without deciding anything. Nothing needs a verdict this week. What you know, you know the way water knows the shore. Going one layer deeper into it is how the pattern underneath shows itself, and you will feel whether it wants to be seen.
cells.sheetLine: You are not deciding yet, and you are not behind.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before moving

cells.tense: You are bracing for an ending that has not happened, and the bracing has started to cost you.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Name something already finished or already changed, and gather in writing what it gave you — three things, no more. Nothing to fix. Just count it, and stop there.
cells.core:
A calm that used to sit easy is running ahead of itself now. You are keeping the feeling level by getting ready for what comes next, and the getting-ready has taken over the room. What was steady has become guarded, and the present shrinks because you are standing one step in front of it.

Name something already finished or already changed, and gather what it gave you — three things, in writing, no more than three. Not what you learned about yourself, just what it left in your hands. Harvesting is the thing your bracing keeps skipping: something did in fact come out of it. Let yourself receive that before you brace for the next one.
cells.sheetLine: You are braced for an ending that has not arrived.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before moving

cells.tense: A door is behind you already, and you are still standing in front of it.
cells.act: gather the scattered thoughts into one line
cells.ask: Put the scattered pieces of what you are deciding onto one page, then write one line that gathers them. Reading it once is the end of the exercise; no acting on it this week.
cells.core:
Where you feel the calm, the feeling has thinned and you are still waiting at something that closed. The present does not feel like a place you can stand, so your mind is spread across several unfinished rooms at once, and none of them gets a full person. Nothing is arriving in you because most of you is somewhere behind.

Put the pieces onto one page, then write a single line that gathers them. Sort them into a shape, not a plan. You are not deciding anything this week; you are bringing the scattered thinking into one place so it stops being several places. Your sense of what is fair to whom gets lost when the thinking is spread thin. One line gives it back some weight.
cells.sheetLine: Your mind is spread across several rooms at once.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before moving

cells.tense: You are keeping things level with other people, and you are the one who does not count it as yours.
cells.act: follow the thought past where it is comfortable
cells.ask: When the thought next runs toward other people, follow it one step further than feels polite, and keep the sentence it lands on. Do not act on it, do not read it to anyone.
cells.core:
You hold other people's weight fairly — you can put the true thing plainly and stay standing — and you do not name that as a strength you have. It gets called just being reasonable. Underneath, there is real thinking going on about distance and closeness and how much anybody should ask of anyone, and you leave it unattributed, so it circulates without an owner.

When the thought next runs toward other people, follow it one step further than feels polite, and keep the sentence it lands on. Hold it somewhere private. Authorship is what this is about: the thinking is already yours, and one sentence kept in your own hand is how you stop lending it to the room.
cells.sheetLine: The thinking is yours already and you have not signed it.
cells.verb: sitting with what the heart knows before moving

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's steadiness is felt by others as a floor — the record gives the capacity and its bend but not who stands on it. The reader could reasonably say no one is leaning on them, or that the wave-off is just manners, not a disowned word; still true that something they hold level is being made smaller than it is. The ask survives being wrong: counting what an ending gave you is useful whether or not the calm is doing more than they say. The sentence that serves me more than them: 'the people who lean on it haven't' — that is the exemplar's move, not this person's, and it gets cut.
